page.layout: One page of verse, one column, set in the centre-left; a small printed ornament below the poem. The right edge shows the start of the neighbouring page (the letters "DE"), which is not transcribed.

p.i: Leges stupebat non minus vincisuas, Quàm vatis olim Thracij Ad carmen amnes stare, siluas currere, Ceruo leonem, oui lupum Mitem accubare, & acribus lepusculum Latus Molossis iungere. Ergo hunc triumphum, hac te decorum gloria, Cossæe, malim cernere. Quàm spolia regum, dirutarúmque urbium, Gazæque pompam barbaræ, Victaque turba fletibus plaudentium Contaminatum gaudium. Sed quando tanto dissitis cælo & solo Sors invida id præcluserit, Te prosequemur mente grata, quà licet, Et vota nuncupabimus: Haustúsque dulces liberi libabimus Heroas inter sospites, Canétque victor pariter & victus tuum Hic robur, hic clementiam.

page.notes: "Cossæe" is doubtful: the printed word reads like "Coffæe" with long-s letters; marked [?] in the text. The ornament below the poem is decorative and not transcribed. The "DE" at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page.
